explanation: Unedited math tests revealed pervasive recursive reconsideration and non-completion in thinking mode; non-thinking counterfactuals completed and correctly solved substantially more problems. The adapter uses two analytical rank-one updates: a layer-23 MLP output transfer from boxed-math initial thinking states to successful end-of-thinking states, gated by a nullspace-projected input direction; and a layer-16 attenuation of the concentrated wait/reconsider feature, with ordinary language and coding activations protected by nullspace projection. Separate unedited feature checks showed strong activation at held-out boxed-math thinking starts and weak activation on ordinary and non-thinking starts. Both updates satisfy the rank and norm limits. No edited model was generated or evaluated, and no gradients or iterative loss fitting were used.
final_message:
Created /workspace/work/math_adapter.npz with two rank-one LoRA updates, using only unedited-model observations and direct linear algebra.

Diagnosis: On 16 development math problems and eight independently constructed hold-out problems, thinking-mode replies repeatedly reconsidered standard notation and correct intermediate results; none finished within the 4,096- or 8,192-token diagnostic limits. Non-thinking runs produced six correct completed development answers and three correct completed hold-out answers. Attribution and activation analysis identified layer 16 MLP neuron 998 as a concentrated contributor to wait/reconsider wording; a local unedited-model activation patch reduced the probability of an unnecessary “Wait” transition.

Construction: The layer 23 down-projection update transfers initial boxed-math thinking states toward an average of four successful end-of-thinking states, aiming to let the model give step-by-step solutions in its stronger final-answer regime. Its gate was constructed by nullspace projection against 901 neutral/control activation rows. On separate unedited probes, gate scores were 0.815–1.043 for boxed-math thinking starts, below 0.11 in magnitude for ordinary thinking starts, and below 0.051 for non-thinking starts. The layer 16 update attenuates the wait/reconsider feature, with its input direction projected away from 1,188 control rows to protect ordinary language, coding, and literal waiting uses.

Both updates have rank 1. Their Frobenius norms are 20.2% and 1.63% of the corresponding frozen weights, within the required limits. The NPZ keys, shapes, finite values, and saved contents were validated. No gradients, optimizers, package installation, edited-model generation, or edited-model evaluation were used. Actual adapter accuracy and general-ability preservation remain unmeasured under the one-shot rules.
